title: La fruta
goal: Buy fruit for the week without paying the chele price
culture: Nothing has a price on it. You ask ¿a cómo?, the first number you are given is the one for a foreigner, and saying está caro is not rudeness — it is the second line of a conversation you are both expected to have.

beats.es: ¡Adelante, mi amor! ¿Qué le doy? Hay mango, papaya, jocote.
beats.objective: Ask the price of the mango
beats.good: ¿A cómo? is the whole question and you will use it every day. Asking is not haggling yet — it is finding out where the haggling starts.

beats.es: A veinte la libra, fresquito, del día.
beats.good: Está caro is neither an insult nor a refusal. It is the line that gets you the real price, and she is waiting for it.

beats.es: Uy. Bueno, se lo dejo a quince. Ni modo.
beats.objective: Ask for a pound of it
ok: una libra de mango por favor
beats.good: Everything on this floor is sold by the libra, and a libra is a pound. The market here never went metric and never will.

beats.es: Ahí le va. ¿Algo más, mi amor?
beats.good: Está bien closes the sale without cutting her off. Mi amor is not flirting — it is what she calls everybody who stops at the stall.
